critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
Clearly better than r1, but not yet fern level. The aisle frame now has a real night setting: bay 2 burns at full level, and four fittings further down glow low. Dawn's head is the brightest thing in the frame that is not a light (best 20 px cell about 175 graded). The aisle floor sits at about 30 and the other travellers' heads at 33-38. That is the lit island r1 asked for. Seat is still the best image: a large, clean profile with soft streaks behind. Nothing clips in any graded frame (max 216/218/215), and black is under control (pixels under 8/255 by Rec. 709 luma: 7.9%, 11.0% and 4.7%).

What still holds it back:
(1) The reflection in seat does not read as Dawn. In the glass her hair dome (about 40) is darker than her face (about 49), and the bun drops to about 23. On Dawn herself, hair and face are close in value (about 140 and 155). The blur turns the dark bun into a swept peak behind the head, so the glass shows a pale face under a cap: another passenger.
(2) In aisle she sits almost square to the camera and looks down the carriage toward the lens, not out of her window. LOOK is 2.8 m ahead and only 0.06 m beyond the glass, which turns her head only about 8 degrees. The stone figure seems to stare back at the viewer.
(3) At aisle scale a zip pull on her suitcase reads as the numeral "3" (about x 290, y 295). That breaks the rule against anything letter-like.
(4) Rack is still a product shot. The case sits a little left of centre against a flat dark wall. The right third holds only wall, bars and the dark window below the rack. There is no carriage beyond, no Dawn, no lit lamp and no motion. The camera comment says the lamp shows below the rail, but it cannot: the lens faces down under the reading-light rail (z about 1.74), and the camera is at 2.08. The case's telescopic handle sticks out about 13 cm, which nobody leaves out on a rack.
(5) In seat a cool passing streak runs straight into the tip of her nose (a tangent). It is one of the random streaks from st.outside(), not a hero streak.

By frame: seat about 6.5, aisle about 6, rack about 5. The frames are clean but sparse, well short of the dense, layered detail of the reference stills.
answers:
C31: THE BUILDER'S THREE QUESTIONS

1) Do Dawn and her reflection read as the same person? Not reliably. It is closer than r1: the reflection is now a profile facing the same way she does, a little over half her size, and at about 31% of her face's value (mean 49 against 157). Those three things are right. What breaks it is the value pattern and the silhouette:
- On Dawn herself, the stone hair cap and the face are close in value (hair about 140, face about 155): one stone.
- In the glass the hair dome falls to about 40 and the bun to about 23, while the face holds at about 49. The glass sees her window side. face_fill lights that side of the face from the front and below. Only the reading lamp reaches the window side of the dome, and it hangs above her on her aisle side (lamp at x -1.035, her eyes at about -1.19). bun_rim lights the bun from the aisle side. So the dome reads as a slightly darker cap. The bun, at under half the face's value and blurred, becomes a swept peak behind the head.
- The result is a narrower, more angular head under a cap. A viewer reads another passenger in a soft cap, not her.
- The streaks frame the reflection without crossing its face (keep_clear removes the two that would). Its seat and shoulders are physically plausible, which also makes it read as somebody sitting behind the glass.
Fix the hair and bun values in the glass (fix 1) and it should read as her.

2) Does the seated figure anchor the aisle? By value, yes. By story, no.
- Value: her face is the brightest object that is not a light. Best 20 px cell about 175; head box mean about 120, p90 174. That is about 6x the aisle floor (about 30) and about 4.5-5x the other heads (Dozer about 34, Sleeper about 38). She sits about a quarter of the way across the frame, left of the third line, under the one fully lit bay. This is the main gain over r1.
- The covers: the linen covers around her run about 100-135, so pale blocks at up to about 75% of her value sit right next to her head and split the attention. On the right, the covers run about 95-105.
- Gesture: her head is turned only about 8 degrees, so from this camera she is near-frontal and looks down the carriage toward the lens. A wide that should read 'a woman looking out at the dark' reads 'a statue staring at us'.
- The suitcase above her, the link to the next shot, reads only as a dark box (mean about 33 against the wall at 18-29). The one detail that does read on it is a zip pull that looks like the numeral '3'.
- The attendant still stands in the vanishing point, framed by the far door. She is darker now (mean 22). But her pale stone legs (up to about 80) under the skirt and her static, hip-width stance, with the feet side by side, make it unclear whether she is walking or which way she faces.
- The passing streaks in the windows barely register. The warm streaks in the right-hand windows peak at about 50-75, and none reads in the left-hand windows: the bay 2 left streak is aimed at z 1.62, the very top edge of the opening. So the frame still does not say the train is moving.

3) Does the suitcase rest convincingly on the rack? Mostly, as geometry. As an object it is less convincing.
- Contact: rack_case() lowers the shell until it touches the crowns of the bars, and I see no float or intersection. The case's bottom edge follows the bars in perspective, and the case and its handle cast soft shadows on the wall at its left. That is the main grounding cue, and it works.
- Rigidity: the case stands on its narrow side like a book on a shelf. Its bottom panel is dead straight and rigid, with no give over the bars. A soft case loaded for weeks would bulge a few millimetres between them.
- The bars in front of it are brighter than the bars further along (about 59 against 21 mean), which is physically right for a strip light above on the aisle side. But the bars just in front of its bottom edge keep the same highlights as the bars beyond the case (peaks about 135-165), so the weight is not felt.
- The telescopic handle is out by about 13 cm (about 8 cm of tube and a 5 cm grip, measured on the mesh), with the tubes visible. Nobody leaves it out on a rack, and it shows the case as a placed prop.
- One case is right for script v2: the extra bag is bought in Ch 04, as COVERAGE.md says. Only stale comments still mention two bags: the docstring of train_set.luggage() ('Dawn's two') and the rack camera comment ('both silhouettes').

WHAT EACH CAMERA'S BEAT STILL NEEDS
- aisle (Ch 03, 'about nine more days'): her head turned to the black window (three-quarter), the covers beside her pushed down, the suitcase above her readable as hers without the '3', a visible passing light in her window, and the attendant out of the vanishing point.
- seat (her face faint in the black glass): the window side of her hair and the bun lit, so the reflection is one stone like her; no streak running into her face; ideally less of the egg-shaped dome lit at full value.
- rack (her one suitcase, the carriage soft beyond): a frame with depth (the rack and carriage receding to soft, distant strips); a tie to her (the top of her head in the reading lamp's pool below the rail, since the lamp's lens faces down and cannot be seen from above the rail); the handle stowed; and some give in the soft case.

fixes.problem: The reflection reads as a different person in a cap. In the glass the hair dome is about 40 and the bun about 23, against a face of about 49. On Dawn herself, hair and face are close in value (about 140 and 155). The blur turns the dark bun into a swept peak behind the head.
fixes.fix: In set_cameras(), after bun_rim, add a window-side hair light: p = eyes + Vector((-0.16, 0.02, 0.2)); st.area('hair_glass', tuple(p), (0.14, 0.14), 1.8, st.LAMP, spread=60, rot=((eyes + Vector((0, 0.1, 0.1))) - p).to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()). st.area() already makes area lights invisible to glossy rays, so the light itself will not show in the glass. Light-link it to Dawn's body mesh and her hair mesh (<body>_hair) only, using a receiver collection as done for bag_edge, so the glass and seats do not brighten. Set it to 0 in TRIMS for aisle and rack. Lower face_fill on seat to about 2.2 (TRIMS['seat']['face_fill'] = 0.73). Targets in the graded seat frame: reflected hair dome at least 0.9x the reflected face (about 45), bun at least 35, real face mean still above 140, and the real crown no brighter than now (see the last fix). Then check in a crop that the bun reads in the glass as a round knot behind the ear, not a peak.

fixes.problem: Dawn looks down the carriage toward the lens. LOOK is 2.8 m ahead and only 0.06 m beyond the glass, which turns her head only about 8 degrees, so the wide reads as a statue staring at the viewer, not a woman looking out of her window.
fixes.fix: Keep the Sitter: in place_dawn() set _STATE['dawn_sitter'] = s. In apply_camera(), when name == 'aisle', call aim_head(_STATE['dawn_sitter'], Vector((GLASS_X - 1.2, SEAT_Y - 1.6, 1.12)), base_turn=(-10, -22)). From her eyes (about x -1.19, y SEAT_Y + 0.13) that point lies about 42 degrees toward the glass. The aisle camera sits about 15 degrees to her aisle side, so it sees a three-quarter view against the black window. A point at SEAT_Y - 1.0 would turn her about 54 degrees, close to profile. For every other camera, call aim_head(sitter, LOOK) again, because the seat camera, its streaks and keep_clear() were set up from her eyes in that pose. Re-run settle_hands() after each re-aim. Then check that the hands still rest in her lap and that her face is still the brightest thing in the aisle frame that is not a light.

fixes.problem: The linen covers around her run about 100-135 graded, up to about 75% of her face. These pale blocks split attention from the only lit face. On the right, the covers run about 95-105.
fixes.fix: In apply_camera('aisle'), darken st.M['linen'] to about 0.55 of its value (0.24 to about 0.13). Its colour comes through a chain of mix nodes in train_mats.linen(), so insert a Multiply node (Mix, MULTIPLY) before Base Color and set its factor per camera (1.0 for seat and rack). For the right-hand covers, trim the near right strip for aisle only with TRIMS['aisle']['strip_R2_light'] = 0.57 (0.35 to 0.2). Do not change LEVELS: that would also dim the strip's diffuser and affect every camera. Target in the graded aisle frame: every cover at or below 80, so her face (best cell about 175) is at least 2x any cover.

fixes.problem: A zip pull on the suitcase reads as the numeral '3' (about x 285-295, y 285-305 in the graded aisle frame). This breaks the rule against anything letter-like. The suitcase itself (mean about 33) barely separates from the rack and wall, so it does not tie her to her luggage.
fixes.fix: In apply_camera('aisle'), give the meshes in _STATE['bag_meshes'] a material variant whose Base Color runs through a Map Range (0.18-1.0 to 0.05-0.09) after the texture. This drops the pale pulls to the charcoal fabric's value and flattens the case, which is fine at this scale. Restore the original materials for the rack camera. Or turn the case so that its pulls face the wall in this view. To lift the case off the wall without the pulls, set TRIMS['aisle']['bag_edge'] to about 0.5; the light is already linked to the bags only, but it is created only when the rack camera is in the build. Target: the case's top edge at 70-90 graded and its body at about 40.

fixes.problem: A product shot. The case sits against a flat dark wall, the right third holds only wall, bars and the dark window below the rack, and there is no carriage beyond, no Dawn, no lit lamp and no motion. The camera comment says the lamp shows below the rail. It cannot: the lens faces down under the reading-light rail (PSU_BOT, z about 1.74), and the camera is at 2.08.
fixes.fix: Look along the carriage instead of at the wall. In set_cameras(), replace the lines that override CAMERAS['rack'] aim and lens (lens 53) with loc about (0.35, SEAT_Y - 1.4, 1.98), aim about (-0.95, SEAT_Y + 1.4, 1.82), lens 40 and fstop 2.8, and keep the focus on fx_bags at the case's aisle-side front. By my projection, the case then sits left of centre in the upper half, and the rack, its brackets and the far bay 7 strips (level 0.18) recede on the right. The top of Dawn's head, out of focus and lit by the reading lamp's pool, lands near the lower-left corner; if it falls out of frame, lower the aim point slightly. Do not count on the lamp's lens: no camera above the rail can see it. Correct the camera comment too. For motion, apply_camera() hides the aisle_motion streaks for every camera but aisle. Leave one visible for rack, or add one through the bay 3 left window, whose glass shows below the rack from this height. Render once at the final settings to check the framing.

fixes.problem: The telescopic handle is out by about 13 cm, with the tubes visible. The soft case sits on the bars as a rigid block with a straight bottom. It looks placed, not set down.
fixes.fix: The case is one fused Tripo mesh (dawn-suitcase.glb), but the handle is the only geometry beyond the shell's top: above about +0.32 on the case's up axis in the unscaled file, where the case is 1.0 tall and the shell top is at about +0.30. In rack_case(), select those vertices in the mesh's local frame and move them back along that axis by about 0.18 unscaled (0.12 m at size 0.66), so the grip sits about 1 cm proud of the shell like a stowed handle. Turning the case end for end would not help: it only moves the handle to the far end, which is still in frame. Optional and lower priority: a lattice on the panel that rests on the bars, so it sags 3-5 mm between them. rack_case() reads o.data.vertices, the undeformed mesh, so read the evaluated mesh when re-running the contact solve after any deform.

fixes.problem: A cool streak runs into the tip of her nose (graded about x 680, y 495) and disappears behind her face: a line running into the profile. It is not hero streak 1, which is the lower cool streak ending short of her jaw at about x 620-650, y 585-590.
fixes.fix: Projected from the code's own camera setup, the culprit is a random streak from st.outside(seed=7): streak_12, cool, strength 3.2. It runs from off the left edge at about y 583 to about x 914, y 478, so it passes behind her head at the nose. keep_clear() only tests the reflection. Extend it with a second keep-out ellipse around her nose tip: take the body vertex furthest along head_forward() from eye_centre() and project it through the seat camera; about 0.04 by 0.05 frame units. Test each streak's whole path, as keep_clear() already does for the reflection, not its end point: the visible end of this streak is where her face covers it. Leave the hero streaks as they are.

fixes.problem: The attendant still stands in the vanishing point, framed by the far door. Her pale stone legs (up to about 80) under the skirt and her feet side by side, hip-width apart, make it unclear whether she is walking or which way she faces. The streaks in the windows barely register: the right-hand ones peak at about 50-75, and none reads on the left. So nothing says the train is moving.
fixes.fix: Hide her for aisle with hide_render in apply_camera(), the way the aisle_motion streaks are toggled. Or move her into the vestibule behind the door glass at about (0.06, 17.9): the vestibule floor runs from y 17.36 to 18.96, so (0.06, 16.6) would still be inside the carriage. She stays on the centre line either way, so hiding her is the surer fix. Do not narrow the stride: the foot_ik offsets (0.13 / -0.11) run along the aisle and barely show from behind, and a shorter stride would read even more as standing. Raise the aisle_motion streak strength from 3.8 to about 7. Lower the bay 2 left streak from z 1.62, the top edge of the opening (TOP = 1.62), to about 1.25, so it crosses her own pane beside her face. Target: each streak at least 110 graded in its window.

fixes.problem: In close-up her cranium reads oversized and egg-shaped, lit near full value (cap about 140), with a hard stepped hairline running from the forehead to behind the ear. It reads more as a swim cap than as sculpted hair.
fixes.fix: Light the crown less than the face, for seat only. In apply_camera(), aim the reading lamp at READING_TARGET with z lowered from 1.15 to about 1.02, and set TRIMS['seat']['reading_lamp'] = 0.8, so the dome falls off toward the back (target cap mean about 115-125, face about 150). Check this together with fix 1: hair_glass and the lower face_fill also change these values. This keeps the one stone finish while the face carries the frame. Report the hard hairline step and the dome's volume as a shared-cast issue in noir-kit/cast.py (_hair, relax_sculpted_hair) rather than patching it here.
